ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

2. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. quickly
   C. blue
   D. run

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

5. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only a joining word

6. When practising Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

7. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. goes
   D. going

8. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

9. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

10. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

11. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

12. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the Library

13. When practising Speaking Fluency: pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

14. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.

15. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Word Class: Determiners: Quantifiers: and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
